summary.tpReason: A high-confidence multi-host sequence associated with jliu corroborates the alert: execution of report.exe, LSASS-dump commands, document staging, SMB administrative-share use, and two vssadmin shadow-copy deletion attempts. On srv-dc01 the destructive command was explicitly blocked/killed and quarantined, but the activity is sufficiently suspicious to require incident handling despite this alert's false_positive/dismissed status.
summary.fpReason: Falcon records this specific detection as false_positive and the invoked binary is the legitimate Windows vssadmin.exe; shadow-copy deletion can be administrative. No Windows SecurityEvent records were available to independently validate the process lineage, logon source, or actual shadow-copy changes. The surrounding jliu activity and unusual command sequence weigh strongly against a routine administrative use.
summary.whatHappened: At 2026-08-15 14:48:39Z, CONTOSO\jliu (jliu@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com) launched C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe on PKWORK\srv-dc01 (10.0.0.10; Falcon agent cs-aid-srvdc01-0006) as `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet`. Falcon reported parent cmd.exe (parent command line `C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe -k netsvcs`), then blocked/killed the process and quarantined it. The server remained online/normal at 15:35Z with prevention policy applied and no filesystem containment. jliu also generated detections on srv-file01 and it-ws01 from 14:36Z–15:25Z: LSASS dump attempts, report.exe execution from Downloads, document staging, SMB admin-share use, and a second blocked vssadmin attempt on srv-file01 at 14:43Z. This is part of wider concurrent suspicious activity across endpoints.
keyEvidence: CrowdStrikeDetections: srv-dc01 detection ldt:cs-aid-srvdc01-0006:874255475204292408 at 14:48:39Z records jliu running `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet`; disposition was "Blocked and Killed" and Quarantined=true.
CrowdStrikeAlerts and CrowdStrikeDetections both classify the srv-dc01 event as ransomware/Impact/T1486 with 72 confidence, although their status is false_positive and Sentinel shows Dismissed.

CrowdStrikeDetections: jliu had 13 detections across srv-file01, it-ws01, and srv-dc01 between 14:36:39Z and 15:25:51Z, including LSASS dumping, report.exe execution, staging, SMB use, and shadow-copy deletion.
CrowdStrikeDetections: srv-file01 had the same vssadmin delete-shadows command under jliu at 14:43:51Z, also blocked/killed and quarantined.
CrowdStrikeHosts: srv-dc01 was normal and last seen at 15:35:27Z; Falcon prevention policy was applied and filesystem containment was normal.
researchDone: Queried CrowdStrikeAlerts for the alert agent/time; confirmed the alert is vendor-status false_positive and Sentinel-status Dismissed, with no recorded resolution duration.
Queried the full CrowdStrike detection for srv-dc01 and host state for cs-aid-srvdc01-0006; obtained command line, account, process lineage, prevention disposition, IPs, and policy/health state.
Reviewed CrowdStrike detections from 14:30Z–15:40Z across the environment and aggregated detections for jliu; found corroborating multi-stage activity on srv-file01 and it-ws01.
Searched SecurityEvent for srv-dc01 and jliu from 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-17; no matching Windows event telemetry was present.

Reviewed Sentinel SecurityAlert records around the incident; found concurrent ransomware detections on other endpoints and a separate medium vulnerability alert for srv-dc01, but no independent confirmation that shadow copies were removed.
Reviewed CrowdStrikeCases in the time window; only an earlier closed auto-created case was returned, with no case linking this srv-dc01 ransomware detection.
